name: Physical Therapist Assistant
description: Physical therapist assistants deliver the treatment a physical therapist has planned — guiding exercise, applying manual therapy and modalities, measuring what has changed, and keeping a discouraged patient working through the months that recovery actually takes. ⚠ A median of $68,380 on a two-year associate degree, with federal growth projected at 17% over 2025–35. ⚠⚠ Check which wage figure you are reading: the federal page covers assistants AND aides together, and an aide earns half as much and needs no degree. ⚠⚠⚠ Florida licenses this work under Chapter 486, and there are two examinations.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠ Florida licensure (s. 486.102, F.S.) needs a CAPTE-accredited associate degree and TWO examinations, and people routinely budget for only one. FIRST, the degree must come from a programme accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE) — the accreditation is what makes you eligible, not the credit. SECOND, the National Physical Therapy Examination for the PTA, taken through the FSBPT at $485. THIRD, a separate Florida Laws and Rules Examination, also through the FSBPT, at $65. The state application and licensing fee is $180, and electronic fingerprinting is required following HB 975. ⚠ Renewal is 24 contact hours every two years — 22 general, 2 on prevention of medical errors, and 1 on HIV/AIDS at first renewal — with no more than 12 hours by home study. ⚠⚠ One provision worth knowing before you graduate: Florida issues a TEMPORARY PERMIT to a United States–trained graduate, valid for six months from graduation, requiring proof of medical malpractice insurance and direct supervision by a licensed physical therapist. It means you can start work while the examination and licence are pending — ask your programme how its graduates use it.
bodyHtml:
What the work actually is

O*NET, on physical therapist assistants: instruct, motivate, safeguard, and assist patients as they practice exercises or functional activities; document patient information, such as notes on their progress; observe patients during treatments to compile and evaluate data on their responses; administer active or passive manual therapeutic exercises, therapeutic massage, aquatic physical therapy; transport patients to and from treatment areas, lifting and transferring them.

⚠ The therapist evaluates and writes the plan; the assistant delivers it. That division is set by statute rather than by custom, and it shapes the job: you spend far more time with each patient than the therapist does, over weeks or months, and you are the person who notices that something has changed.

⚠⚠ It is physical work. Transferring and lifting patients is in the task list for a reason, and so is the emotional side — a great deal of the skill is keeping someone working at something difficult and slow when they can no longer see it helping.

⚠⚠⚠ Read the wage figure carefully — the federal page covers two different jobs

The BLS publishes assistants and aides on one page, and the headline number is the blend of both. They are not the same job.

Role2025 medianNeeds a degree?Licensed?
Physical therapist ASSISTANT$68,380yes — CAPTE associateyes
Physical therapist AIDE⚠ $35,240nono
combined figure the page leads with$61,200——

⚠ If you search for this career you will meet the $61,200 or the $35,240 first, and both will mislead you. The number attached to the credential this page describes is $68,380. An aide sets up equipment and cleans it; an assistant treats patients.

Projected need — and both sources agree it is fast

  • O*NET (2024–34 projections): 111,500 employed as assistants, growth much faster than average (7% or higher), 19,800 openings a year, median $68,380 (2025).
  • BLS OOH (2025–35 projections, assistants and aides together): 163,200 jobs, growth 17%, much faster than average, employment change +28,200.

✅ They agree, and 17% is at the top of the range of anything on this site. ⚠⚠ Note the openings figure against the employment figure — 19,800 a year against 111,500 assistants is close to one opening per six people employed, every year. That is a field with real hiring, and it is the practical reason the credential is worth having.

⚠⚠ Physics is in the prerequisites, and people are caught by it

Most Florida PTA programmes require anatomy and physiology with laboratories, psychology, and a physics course — Indian River State College's 74-credit A.S. names PHY 1020 Principles of Physics or higher alongside both halves of anatomy and physiology.

⚠ That surprises applicants who chose a health programme expecting to avoid it, and it is not decoration: levers, force, torque and friction are what therapeutic exercise and manual therapy are made of, and the biomechanics course assumes them. Take it seriously and take it early — it is the prerequisite most likely to delay an application by a term.

⚠⚠ Everything requires a grade of C or higher, and admission is limited-access at every Florida programme, so the prerequisite grades are the application.

⚠⚠ Two different suffix patterns live in this prefix, and the difference matters

This prefix is an unusually clean illustration of a distinction that costs students credit elsewhere on this site. Both shapes are present, and the diagnostic is who carries what.

PairCarriersWhat it means
PHT 1200 + PHT 1200L
Basic Patient Care		✅ the same 7 institutions carry botha genuine lecture-plus-laboratory pair — enrol in both halves in the same term
PHT 2810 vs PHT 2810L
Clinical Practice II		⚠ 6 institutions vs 11, no overlap at allone course filed two ways by different colleges — same content, different identifier
PHT 2820 vs PHT 2820L⚠ 6 vs 9, no overlapthe same, on the next clinical course
PHT 2162 vs PHT 2162C
Neurological conditions		⚠ 6 vs 6, no overlapthe same, on the neurology course

⚠⚠⚠ An evaluator matching on the identifier sees a mismatch on three of these four where there is none. The rule to carry away: if the same college carries both forms it is a packaging split and you take both; if different colleges carry different forms, it is one course with two filings.

⚠ The numbers do not travel, so plan for that

Florida carries 171 lower-division physical therapy course numbers across 21 institutions, and the most widely shared real course — Clinical Practice II — reaches only 11 of the 21. Programmes name the same subjects differently: Principles of Practice at one college, Basic Patient Care at another, Therapeutic Modalities at a third.

⚠⚠ So do not plan to assemble the programme from courses at several colleges. These are cohort programmes taken as a designed sequence; what transfers between colleges is the general education and the science prerequisites, not the professional courses. Take the prerequisites anywhere convenient and the programme in one place.

⚠ The assistant degree is not a step toward being a therapist

Florida has 17 public institutions awarding the assistant associate degree and 7 awarding the Doctor of Physical Therapy — and the state produces more therapists (350 a year) than assistants (267).

⚠⚠⚠ The associate degree does not shorten the doctorate. A PTA who decides to become a PT completes a bachelor's degree and then applies to a DPT programme in open competition. That is a seven-year route rather than a continuation, and it is the single most common misunderstanding about this career. If being the therapist is the goal, look hard at going straight for the bachelor's-then-DPT route now.

⚠ What the assistant credential does offer is two years to a licensed clinical job with real hiring, in a field where much of the day-to-day patient contact belongs to you rather than to the therapist. That is a good job on its own terms — just choose it as a destination rather than as a waypoint.

Necessary skills

  • Applied anatomy you can see and feel. Knowing which muscle is not firing, by watching someone walk, is the craft.
  • Physical stamina and safe body mechanics. You transfer patients, and the injuries that end careers in this field are the ones you cause yourself.
  • Coaching under discouragement. Progress is slow and often invisible week to week; sustaining someone's effort through that is most of the therapeutic effect.
  • Precise observation and documentation. Your notes are what the therapist uses to change the plan of care, and what the insurer uses to keep paying for it.
  • Knowing the edge of your scope. The statute puts evaluation and the plan of care with the therapist; recognising when something has changed enough to need one is a skill in itself.

Advice

⚠ Check CAPTE accreditation first, at capteonline.org. It is what makes you eligible to sit the national examination, and no other statement on a college's page substitutes for it.

⚠⚠ Budget for both examinations and the fees. The NPTE is $485, the Florida Laws and Rules examination is $65, and the state application is $180 — roughly $730 after a two-year degree, and programmes do not always say so up front.

⚠ Ask about the temporary permit. Six months from graduation, with malpractice insurance and direct supervision, is enough to be earning while the licence is processed. Programmes whose graduates use it routinely will tell you how.

And spend a day in an outpatient clinic and a day in a skilled nursing facility before you choose. They are both PTA jobs and they are barely the same work — one is athletes and post-surgical knees, the other is frail older people and slow, arduous gains. Most students have only pictured the first.

programs.note: The programme itself, at both levels — 17 Florida public institutions for the assistant associate degree and 7 for the doctorate. ⚠ Read its degrees note before assuming the two connect: the associate is not advanced standing toward the DPT, and Florida produces more therapists than assistants.

⚠ Not a route here — separate credentials, neither transfers. Named because it is the other two-year limited-access programme at the same colleges and the comparison is close: radiography pays more at entry ($80,110 against $68,380) and is procedural and scheduled, where this work is longitudinal and physical.

⚠ Not a route here. Named because it is at 78 Florida institutions against 17, so for many students it is the programme that actually exists nearby — and because people who want sustained contact with the same patients over months often find this work suits them better than shift-based nursing does.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I — 20 institutions. Required by Florida PTA programmes with a grade of C or higher, and the course admission is largely decided on.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Two equivalent packagings: 20 institutions split it into BSC2085 plus BSC2085L, and 7 carry the combined BSC2085C. Register for whichever your catalogue lists, and where it is split take BOTH halves in the same term.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I Laboratory — 19 institutions, the corequisite half.
Anatomy and Physiology II — 19 institutions. The second half, required alongside the first by every Florida PTA programme checked.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also carried as the combined BSC2086C at 7 institutions.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology II Laboratory — 19 institutions.

Principles of Physics — 21 institutions. ⚠ The prerequisite applicants do not expect in a health programme, and it is required: Indian River names PHY1020 or higher. Levers, force and torque are what therapeutic exercise is built on.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ 'Or higher' matters if you may later go on to a bachelor's and a DPT — PHY2053 General Physics I (19 institutions) satisfies the PTA requirement AND counts toward a science degree, where the survey course often does not. ⚠ Check whether your programme wants the laboratory too.

courses.reason: Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. Required outright rather than as an option at Indian River, because adherence, motivation and pain behaviour are half of whether a plan of care works.
English Composition I — 39 institutions, in the general-education core of every Florida PTA associate degree.
College Algebra — 36 institutions. One of the mathematics options, and the one to take if a bachelor's degree is a possibility later.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Programmes usually allow a choice: Indian River accepts College Algebra or higher, Mathematical Thinking, Elementary Statistics or Calculus I. Check your own college's list.

courses.reason: Introduction to Physical Therapy — 6 institutions. The profession, the scope of practice, the legal division between therapist and assistant, and the settings the work happens in.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Several colleges instead open with PHT1200 Basic Patient Care (7 institutions) or a course called Principles of Practice I. The prefix names the same subjects differently at nearly every college.

courses.reason: Basic Patient Care — 7 institutions. Transfers, positioning, vital signs, body mechanics and safety: the skills used on the first day of the first clinical placement.
courses.variantNote: ✅ A genuine lecture-plus-laboratory pair — the SAME 7 institutions carry PHT1200 and PHT1200L, so take both halves together. ⚠ Contrast this with the clinical courses on this page, where different colleges carry different suffixes for one course.

courses.reason: Basic Patient Care Laboratory — 7 institutions, the hands-on half where the transfers are actually practised on each other.
Functional Anatomy and Kinesiology — 3 institutions under this number. How joints and muscles produce movement, and the course the physics prerequisite exists to support.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Carried under this number at only 3 colleges but taught at all of them under names such as Kinesiology, Applied Anatomy or Functional Anatomy. This is the course to compare when checking whether a programme's sequence matches another's.

courses.reason: Medical Surgical Conditions — 5 institutions. The pathology behind the referrals: what was repaired, what is healing, and what the treatment must not do yet.
Foundations of Therapeutic Exercise — 3 institutions under this number. Prescribing and progressing exercise, which is the core intervention of the whole profession.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also carried as PHT2220C Therapeutic Exercise in P.T. (4 institutions) and PHT2228C Therapeutic Exercise II (4). Three numbers, one subject, different colleges.

courses.reason: Therapeutic Modalities — the agents applied alongside exercise: heat, cold, ultrasound, electrical stimulation and traction, with the evidence for each.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Titled Principles of Practice III at Indian River and Therapeutic Modalities elsewhere. ⚠⚠ Expect the evidence base for several modalities to be contested — a good programme teaches which ones current guidelines still support.

courses.reason: Survey of Neurological Deficiencies — 6 institutions. Stroke, spinal cord injury, Parkinson's and brain injury: the caseload in rehabilitation hospitals and much of skilled nursing.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Carried as PHT2162 at 6 colleges and PHT2162C at 6 others, with NO college carrying both — one course, two filings. ⚠ Also taught as PHT2255 Neuromuscular PT at colleges using a different sequence.

courses.reason: Cardiopulmonary and Systemic Physical Therapy — the cardiac and pulmonary rehabilitation side, plus the systemic conditions that change what a patient can tolerate.
Clinical Practice I — 6 institutions. The first supervised placement, usually short, where the laboratory skills meet a real caseload.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ A clinical course: full-time hours in a clinic on its schedule, not the college's. Expect Level 2 background screening, immunisations, TB and drug screening, health insurance and current CPR to be complete BEFORE the placement, and expect to travel to it.

courses.reason: Clinical Practice II — 11 institutions, the most widely carried real course in the prefix. A full-time placement at which you are treating a caseload under supervision.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Filed as PHT2810 without the L at 6 other colleges, and the carrier sets do NOT overlap — one course, two identifiers. An evaluator matching on the number sees a difference that is not there.

courses.reason: Clinical Practice III — 9 institutions, the terminal placement. Its competency record is what a first employer asks about and what the examination assumes you have done.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Filed as PHT2820 without the L at 6 other colleges, again with no overlap. ⚠ Keep the clinical performance instrument and the hour log; the transcript line will not describe what you did.

sources.label: Section 486.102, Florida Statutes — physical therapist assistant licensing
sources.note: ⚠ The licence requirements: a degree from a programme approved for the education of physical therapist assistants by the appropriate recognised accrediting agency, and passing a board-approved examination. Renewal requires 24 hours of continuing education biennially.

sources.label: Florida Board of Physical Therapy — Physical Therapist Assistant
sources.note: ⚠⚠ TWO examinations, and the fees: the National Physical Therapy Examination at $485 and a separate Florida Laws and Rules Examination at $65, both through the FSBPT, plus a $180 application and licensing fee and electronic fingerprinting under HB 975. ⚠ Also the six-month temporary permit for United States–trained graduates, requiring malpractice insurance and direct supervision.

sources.label: CAPTE — Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education
sources.note: ⚠ Check the programme here before applying. CAPTE accreditation is what the Florida licence route names, and it accredits both the assistant associate degree and the Doctor of Physical Therapy.

sources.note: Assistant (51.0806): 17 Florida public institutions, 267 credentials — Miami Dade 35, Broward 32, St Petersburg 25, FSCJ 24. ⚠ Therapist (51.2308): 7 institutions, 350 doctorates — so Florida produces MORE therapists than assistants.

Also 171 lower-division numbers across 21 institutions, with the most shared real course reaching 11.
